definitions.explanation: The natural and physical sciences — typically mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, and earth science as an academic grouping, distinct from engineering or the humanities.

examples.japanese: {理学|りがく}{部|ぶ}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: To enter the faculty of science.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{理学|りがく}{博士|はかせ}{号|ごう}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: She holds a doctorate in science.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}{進学|しんがく}の{際|さい}、{工学|こうがく}と{理学|りがく}のどちらにするか{迷|まよ}った。
examples.english: When applying to university, I agonized over whether to choose engineering or science.

notes:
Used mainly in academic/institutional names rather than as a stand-alone term in conversation.

COMPOUNDS:
- {理学|りがく}{部|ぶ}: faculty/school of science (at a university)
- {理学|りがく}{博士|はかせ}: doctor of science (PhD)
- {理学|りがく}{療法|りょうほう}: physical therapy
- {理学|りがく}{療法士|りょうほうし}: physical therapist

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {科学|かがく}: science — broader, everyday word for 'science' in general
- {工学|こうがく}: engineering — applied/practical, contrasted with {理学|りがく} at universities
- {自然科学|しぜんかがく}: natural sciences — overlaps with {理学|りがく} but more general
